Section 1

What changes in finance at Level 5

Who it is for. Finance managers, financial controllers, payroll managers and procurement leads who run a finance function or a team within one, such as accounts payable, credit control, planning and analysis, payroll or procurement.

Much of a finance team's week is matching, checking and explaining. Invoices are matched to orders. Bank lines are matched to the ledger. Variances are explained in words each month. Tools now take a first pass at each of these. An invoice-matching tool clears the clean matches and queues the rest. AI drafts variance commentary from the ledger. A forecasting tool proposes next quarter's figures from the trend.

The work does not disappear. It moves. The accounts payable clerk who keyed invoices now works the exception queue. The management accountant who wrote commentary now checks a draft against the business. Fewer hours go on processing. More go on judging whether an output is right. That changes what each role needs to be good at, and which mistakes are now possible.

Some things do not move when the tools do. Records must still explain each transaction. The VAT return must still come from digital records. Payroll must still report on time. Duties kept apart must stay apart, even when one tool does both steps. At this level the learner leads their own finance function or team through that shift. How the organisation as a whole runs finance is set above them.

The same qualification. A learner on this version is assessed against the same criteria, to the same assessment model, as a learner on the generic Diploma. Only the context differs. Their own department is the evidence.

Section 3

The rules finance works within

A department changing its work stays inside these. The learner records each one where the units ask for constraints and obligations, and works within it.

Companies Act 2006, accounting records. Records must show and explain each transaction, and any automated step has to leave records that still do. It is a constraint at ZFF-AU-05 1.4 and an obligation at ZFF-PJ-05 1.6, and it shapes the checks at ZFF-AU-05 5.1.

HMRC Making Tax Digital for VAT. VAT records must be kept digitally, and figures must reach the return through digital links. A new tool between ledger and return must keep that chain intact. It is recorded at ZFF-AU-05 1.4 and ZFF-PJ-05 1.6.

HMRC PAYE Real Time Information reporting. Payroll must report pay to HMRC on or before each payday. No change may put that date at risk. It is recorded at ZFF-PJ-05 1.6 and shapes the fallbacks at ZFF-PJ-05 4.5.

UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Payroll, expense and supplier bank records hold personal data. That limits which tools may process them and which data an analysis may use. It is recorded at ZFF-AU-05 1.4 and, where data is set aside, at ZFF-DA-05 2.3.

Segregation of duties and delegated authority limits. Raising, authorising and paying stay with different people, each within an authority limit. An automation that does two of those steps can collapse the separation. It is weighed at ZFF-AU-05 3.5 and 5.1 and at ZFF-PJ-05 4.4.

Audit trail and access for external audit. Auditors need to trace an entry to its source and see who checked it. Each automated step needs that trail. Where the auditor must review a new control first, that is a dependency at ZFF-PJ-05 4.2.

The organisation's own change and consultation procedures. How the department may change people's roles is set by the organisation's procedures and any agreements in place. The learner works within them and records them at ZFF-EI-05 1.5 and ZFF-GM-05 1.4.

ZFF-GM-05

Leading a Department Through a Change in Required Capability

Level5TQT60 hoursCredits6GLH24 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria28

In Finance

In finance this unit is about what the team needs to be good at once tools do the matching and first drafts. An accounts payable team that keyed invoices now needs people who can read an exception queue. A management accounts team now needs people who can test an AI draft against the ledger. The learner establishes what their team can do now and what it will need. They then lead its people through the change.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know how a change in required capability affects the work of a department.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse the effects on a department's work when the capabilities its roles require change, including the effect on people whose established competence is no longer what the work requires
1.2Compare different approaches to building capability in a department, and the reasoning behind each
1.3Evaluate the reasons capability-building programmes fail to change what people do at work
1.4Identify the constraints that limit what own department can change about the capability it holds, including time, budget, role definitions, agreements and the availability of learning
1.5Evaluate the different views held within own department about the change in what its people are expected to be good at, and the reasoning given for them

Applied in Finance

At 1.1 the learner analyses how the team's work changes. That includes a long-serving clerk whose strength was fast, accurate keying. 1.2 and 1.5 ask for the reasoning behind each approach and view, such as formal training against learning on the job. 1.3 looks at why system training can leave people working the old way. 1.4 records constraints such as the close calendar, job grades, agreements and budget.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to establish what capability a department holds and what it will require.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Determine the method used to establish what capability the department holds and what it will require, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.2Establish the capabilities the department's roles currently require, and the work each of those capabilities supports
2.3Establish the capability the department currently holds, using the department's own records and evidence from work already carried out
2.4Determine the capability the department will require as its processes change, and state the reasons
2.5Analyse the difference between the capability held and the capability required, and identify where that difference carries most cost to the department
2.6Evaluate the reliability of the evidence obtained, and state how gaps were handled

Applied in Finance

The learner determines their own method at 2.1. A skills audit form supplied from outside does not meet it. At 2.2 and 2.3 they draw on the team's own records, such as who clears which exceptions and review notes on journals. 2.4 determines what the team will need, such as reviewing tool-matched invoices. 2.5 and 2.6 find where the gap costs most, such as rework at close. They also test how far the records can be trusted.

LO3
The learner will: Be able to determine how a department's capability difference will be closed.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Determine the criteria against which options for closing the difference will be evaluated, and state the reasons for them
3.2Identify the options available for closing each part of the difference, including developing the people already in post, changing how work is allocated, recruiting, redeploying, and obtaining capability from outside the department
3.3Interpret the cost and the benefit of each option, using figures from the department's own systems
3.4Use relevant investigation of comparable work, inside or outside own organisation, to inform the choice between options
3.5Identify a capability the department should not attempt to build, and evaluate the reasons
3.6Evaluate the options against the criteria determined at 3.1, and state which are recommended

Applied in Finance

At 3.1 the learner sets their own criteria, such as cover for the next year end, and cost. 3.2 goes beyond training. Options include reallocating reconciliations, recruiting a systems accountant or borrowing support from another team. 3.3 uses the team's own figures, such as overtime at close. 3.4 draws on how a comparable team handled a similar change. At 3.5 the learner might decide specialist tax capability is better bought in than built.

LO4
The learner will: Be able to lead a department through a change in what its people are expected to be good at.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Identify the people whose expected capability changes, and state how it changes for each
4.2Consult those people about the change, and record what was raised
4.3Analyse the concerns raised, and evaluate which of them alter the recommended options
4.4Adapt the recommendation in response to what the consultation established, and state what changed
4.5State, for each person whose expected capability changes, the actions they are expected to take, the support available to them and the period over which the change applies
4.6Determine how the change in the department's capability will be evidenced in the work the department produces, and state what will count as evidence

Applied in Finance

4.1 and 4.5 name each affected role, such as the purchase ledger clerk or Colleague A. For each they state the actions expected, the support offered and the period. 4.2 and 4.3 record and analyse what people raised. One example is a fear that signing off a tool's matches carries more personal risk than keying. 4.4 shows how the recommendation changed. 4.6 sets what will count as evidence, such as fewer reopened reconciliations.

LO5
The learner will: Be able to evaluate a change in a department's capability and own method.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Evaluate the change in the department's capability against the requirement determined at 2.4, using the evidence determined at 4.6
5.2Evaluate the effect of the change on the work the department produces, using figures from the department's own systems
5.3Identify where the change did not take effect, and evaluate the reasons
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.1 and the criteria determined at 3.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Identify what would be determined differently at the next change in the department's required capability, and the reasons

Applied in Finance

5.1 and 5.2 evaluate the change against 2.4 and the evidence set at 4.6. They use the team's own figures, such as the close timetable or exception ageing. If only one close has passed, the learner evaluates the effect seen so far and states its limits. 5.3 asks where the change did not take hold. 5.4 and 5.5 review the learner's own method and criteria.

5 learning outcomes, 28 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Finance work

  • 2.1, 2.3. A note of the method chosen to establish the team's capability. Extracts from the team's own records support it, such as exception logs by preparer, annotated by the learner.
  • 2.4, 2.5. A statement of what the accounts payable team will need once an invoice-matching tool is live. It sets this against what the team holds now and marks the costliest gap.
  • 3.1, 3.3, 3.6. An options paper built on the learner's own criteria. Each option is costed from the team's overtime and contractor figures, and the recommended options are named.
  • 4.2, 4.3, 4.4. Consultation notes with colleagues identified by role. The learner's analysis of what was raised, and the revised recommendation showing what changed.
  • 4.5. A short plan for each affected role. It states the actions expected, the support available and the period.
  • 5.1, 5.2, 5.3. A review after at least one month-end close. It is set against the evidence determined at 4.6 and states the limits of the period.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when a competency framework or skills matrix from a transformation team defines what the team needs. It also drops when options come from a fixed training list within a set budget. It rises above Level 5 when the learner sets out to redesign finance roles across the organisation, which belongs at 1.4 as a constraint.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-GM-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

ZFF-EI-05

Working with the People Whose Roles Change

Level5TQT60 hoursCredits6GLH24 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria27

In Finance

In finance the people whose roles change are often long-serving and very accurate at the work being automated. A payroll administrator may feel a tool's mistakes will be theirs to answer for. Some people object to the change itself. Others object to how it is made, such as moving to a new tool during year end. The learner works with all of them, including those who do not accept it.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know how people in a department respond when their roles change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse the effects on the work of a department when the roles within it change
1.2Evaluate what is at stake for different groups of people in a department when its roles change, and the reasoning behind the positions they take
1.3Compare different approaches to working with people through a change to their roles, and the reasoning behind each
1.4Evaluate the reasons changes to roles are agreed and then not carried through in practice
1.5Identify the obligations and constraints that govern how own department may work with people whose roles change, including consultation requirements, agreements and the organisation's own procedures

Applied in Finance

1.1 and 1.2 analyse what changes for the team and what is at stake for each group. Clerks may lose keying work while reviewers take on more sign-off risk. 1.3 compares approaches, such as a volunteer pilot against moving everyone at once. 1.4 looks at why agreed changes drift back, such as manual workarounds kept alive at close. 1.5 records the organisation's procedures and any agreements in place.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to establish how a change to roles affects the people in a department.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Identify the people whose roles change and state what changes for each, and identify the people whose work depends on the roles that change
2.2Determine the method used to establish what those people raise about the change, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.3Establish, using that method, what each person or group raises about the change, and record it
2.4Analyse what was raised to establish which points concern the change itself and which concern the way it is being made
2.5Interpret what was raised to establish which parts of the change are least likely to be carried through in practice, and state the reasons
2.6Evaluate the reliability of what the method established, and state how the position of people who did not take part was handled

Applied in Finance

2.1 names each role that changes and the roles that depend on it. Budget holders rely on accounts payable, and employees rely on payroll. 2.2 is the learner's own choice of method, such as one-to-ones for payroll staff. 2.3 records what each person raised. 2.4 separates objections to the change from objections to how it is made. 2.5 finds the parts least likely to stick. 2.6 states how absent views were handled.

LO3
The learner will: Be able to determine how a department will respond to people who do not accept a change.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Determine the criteria against which the department's response to each point raised will be evaluated, and state the reasons for them
3.2Analyse the points raised by people who do not accept the change, and evaluate which of them are supported by evidence
3.3Determine which points will change the department's plans and which will not, and state the reasons in each case
3.4Use relevant investigation of comparable changes, inside or outside own organisation, to inform the response
3.5Adapt the department's plans in line with the points determined at 3.3, and state what changed
3.6Determine what the department will do where a person continues not to accept the change, within the obligations and constraints identified at 1.5

Applied in Finance

3.1 sets the criteria for judging each response, such as whether a point bears on control, accuracy or workload. 3.2 tests objections against evidence. A claim that the tool mishandles credit notes is checked against the exception log. 3.3 and 3.5 decide which points change the plan and record what changed. 3.4 draws on comparable changes. 3.6 decides what happens if someone still does not accept it, within 1.5.

LO4
The learner will: Be able to work with the people whose roles change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1State to each person whose role changes what is changing, when it changes, and what is expected of them
4.2Respond to each point raised, stating what the department will do about it and the reasons
4.3Conduct a discussion with a person who does not accept the change, and record what was agreed and what was not
4.4Determine the support each person requires to carry out the changed role, and state how and when it will be provided
4.5Determine how the department will keep the people whose roles change informed while the change proceeds, and how the effect on their work will be measured

Applied in Finance

4.1 states to each person what is changing and when. Timing works around the close calendar and the payroll cut-off. 4.2 answers each point with what the department will do and why. 4.3 is a recorded discussion with a person who has said they do not accept the change. 4.4 sets support for each changed role. 4.5 sets how people are kept informed and how the effect will be measured.

LO5
The learner will: Be able to evaluate how a department worked with the people whose roles changed.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Evaluate the effect of the change on the work of the people whose roles changed, against what was determined at 4.5
5.2Evaluate the effect of the change on the department's work, using figures from the department's own systems
5.3Evaluate how far the points recorded at 2.3 changed what the department did, giving reasons
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.2 and the criteria determined at 3.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Identify what would be determined differently at the next change to the department's roles, and the reasons

Applied in Finance

5.1 and 5.2 evaluate the effect on the people whose roles changed and on the team's work. They use the team's own figures, such as payroll corrections. 5.3 tests how far the points recorded at 2.3 changed what the team did. 5.4 and 5.5 review the learner's own method and criteria.

5 learning outcomes, 27 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Finance work

  • 2.1. A role map of each finance role that changes and what changes for it. It also shows dependent roles, such as budget holders and employees paid through payroll.
  • 2.2, 2.3, 2.6. The learner's consultation method and the record of what each person or group raised. Colleagues are identified by role, with a note on how absent views were handled.
  • 2.4, 3.2. An analysis sorting objections to the change from objections to how it is made. Each objection is tested against the team's own records.
  • 3.3, 3.5. A decision log stating which points changed the plan and which did not, with reasons. The revised plan sits beside it.
  • 4.3. A record of the discussion with Colleague A, who stated they do not accept the change. It shows what was agreed and what was not, with witness testimony from the line manager.
  • 5.1, 5.2, 5.3. A review after at least one close or payroll cycle. It uses the team's own figures and states the limits of the period covered.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when the learner is handed the people to consult, a briefing script and a fixed list of concessions. It rises above Level 5 when the learner tries to change how the organisation handles role change, such as regrading finance roles across the group. That belongs at 1.5 as a constraint.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-EI-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

ZFF-AU-05

Planning Automation Across a Department

Level5TQT80 hoursCredits8GLH46 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria26

In Finance

In finance this unit asks which parts of purchase-to-pay, the close, credit control or payroll could be automated. It also asks which should not be, and what it would cost to find out. The learner maps what the team does, sets their own criteria, and tests candidates against the team's own figures. Control runs through all of it. Each automated step needs checks, fallbacks and points of human decision.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know how automation changes the work of a department.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse the effects that introducing automation has on the work of the people in a department
1.2Compare different approaches to introducing automation into a department, and the reasoning behind each
1.3Evaluate the reasons automation programmes fail to deliver what was expected of them
1.4Identify the constraints that limit what own department can automate, including systems, contracts, permissions and skills
1.5Evaluate the different views held within own department about automation, and the reasoning given for them

Applied in Finance

1.1 analyses how automation changes a finance team's work, such as a clerk moving from keying to exceptions. 1.2 compares approaches, such as one ledger end to end against one step across all ledgers. 1.3 looks at why finance automations fall short, such as poor supplier master data. 1.4 records constraints such as the finance system, licence terms, user permissions, segregation of duties and the team's skills.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to establish what a department does and where its effort goes.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Map the processes carried out by own department, showing inputs, outputs and the people involved
2.2Determine the method used to establish where the department's effort goes, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.3Establish the volume and the time cost of the department's main processes from the department's own systems
2.4Identify the processes that other teams depend on, and what they depend on them for
2.5Evaluate the reliability of the figures obtained, and state how gaps were handled

Applied in Finance

2.1 maps the team's processes, such as purchase-to-pay from order to payment run. 2.2 determines how to find where effort goes, such as time logs across one close. 2.3 takes volume and time from the team's own systems, such as invoice and manual journal counts. 2.4 finds what other teams depend on, such as budget holders waiting on accruals. 2.5 tests how far the figures can be trusted.

LO3
The learner will: Be able to evaluate processes in a department as candidates for automation.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Determine the criteria against which candidate processes will be evaluated, and state the reasons for them
3.2Analyse a candidate process to establish which parts could be automated and which could not
3.3Interpret the costs and the benefits of automating a candidate process, using figures from the department's own systems
3.4Use relevant investigation of comparable work, inside or outside own organisation, to inform the evaluation
3.5Identify a process that should not be automated, and evaluate the reasons
3.6Evaluate the candidate processes against the criteria determined at 3.1, and state which are recommended

Applied in Finance

At 3.1 the learner sets the criteria a candidate must meet, such as volume, error cost and control risk. 3.2 might split bank reconciliation into automatic matching and human review of the rest. 3.3 costs each candidate from the team's own figures. 3.4 draws on comparable work elsewhere. 3.5 names a process to keep manual, such as releasing the payment run. 3.6 sets out the recommendation.

LO4
The learner will: Be able to work with the people whose work automation would change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Identify the people whose work would change, and how it would change for each
4.2Consult those people about the proposed change, and record what was raised
4.3Analyse the concerns raised, and evaluate which of them alter the evaluation
4.4Adapt the evaluation in response to what the consultation established, and state what changed
4.5Evaluate the skills the department would need that it does not currently hold

Applied in Finance

4.1 and 4.2 identify and consult the people whose work would change. These include purchase ledger clerks, the payments officer and budget holders who authorise invoices. 4.3 tests which concerns alter the evaluation, such as part-delivered orders the tool cannot match. 4.4 records what changed. 4.5 covers only the skills these automations need, such as maintaining matching rules.

LO5
The learner will: Be able to recommend a course of action and evaluate own method.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1State the checks, the fallbacks and the points of human decision for each recommended process
5.2Evaluate the risks the recommendation carries for the department, and what would be done about each
5.3Present the recommendation, with the evidence, to the person who would decide
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.2 and the criteria determined at 3.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Identify what would be determined differently in a further evaluation, and the reasons

Applied in Finance

5.1 states the checks, fallbacks and points of human decision for each process. Examples are a sample review of auto-matched invoices and a manual route before a payment run. 5.2 evaluates risks such as a broken audit trail or a duplicate payment. 5.3 presents to the person who would decide, such as the financial controller. 5.4 and 5.5 review the learner's own method and criteria.

5 learning outcomes, 26 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Finance work

  • 2.1, 2.4. A process map of the team's purchase-to-pay or close processes. It shows inputs, outputs, people and the other teams that depend on each step.
  • 2.2, 2.3, 2.5. Volume and time figures from the finance system and the team's own logs. The learner's note covers the method and the gaps in the figures.
  • 3.1, 3.3, 3.6. An evaluation of candidate processes against the learner's own criteria. It is costed from the team's figures and ends in a recommendation.
  • 3.5. A short case for a process the team should keep manual, such as payment run release, with reasons.
  • 4.2, 4.3, 4.4. Consultation notes with clerks and budget holders identified by role. The revised evaluation shows what changed.
  • 5.1, 5.2, 5.3. The recommendation as presented, with checks, fallbacks and points of human decision for each process. Witness testimony confirms it was presented.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when the learner is handed the processes to evaluate. It also drops when a business case template or control framework fixes what counts as a benefit. It rises above Level 5 when the work becomes a redesign of how the organisation runs finance, such as a shared service centre. That belongs at 1.4 as a constraint.

ZFF-DA-05

Using Data to Direct a Department's Priorities

Level5TQT70 hoursCredits7GLH40 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria25

In Finance

Finance teams report many measures of their own work, such as days to close, debtor days and forecast accuracy. This unit asks what those measures count and what behaviour they encourage. A target on days to close can push accruals towards rough estimates. A count of invoices processed can push hard invoices to the back. The learner then uses the team's own data to decide where its effort should go.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know what a department's measures show and what they drive.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse what the measures reported by own department actually count, and over what period
1.2Analyse the behaviour each measure encourages in the people whose work it reports on
1.3Evaluate what own department's current measures leave out
1.4Compare different approaches to measuring work of this kind, and the reasoning behind each
1.5Evaluate the different views held within own department about what its measures show, and the reasoning given for them

Applied in Finance

1.1 and 1.2 analyse what the team's measures count, over what period, and what they encourage. 1.3 evaluates what they leave out, such as time budget holders spend on queries. 1.4 compares approaches, such as speed against first-time accuracy, with the reasoning behind each. 1.5 sets out the views within the team about what its measures show.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to determine a question about a department's priorities that data could help settle.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Determine the question about own department's priorities that the work will address, and state the reasons for selecting it
2.2Determine the data that bears on the question, and state the reasons for the selection
2.3Identify data that was available but set aside, and evaluate the effect of setting it aside
2.4Determine the method to be used to work with the data, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.5Evaluate the quality of the data obtained, and state how gaps and errors were handled

Applied in Finance

2.1 is the learner's own question. One example is whether credit control should chase by value or by age of debt. 2.2 and 2.3 choose the data and state what was set aside and why. That might be disputes held only in email, or personal data left out under UK GDPR. 2.4 determines the method. 2.5 evaluates data quality, such as duplicate customer accounts.

LO3
The learner will: Be able to analyse a department's data and interpret what it indicates.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Analyse the selected data in relation to the question
3.2Interpret what the analysis indicates about where the department's effort is going
3.3Identify an interpretation the same data would also support, and evaluate which of the two it better supports
3.4Use relevant investigation, inside or outside own organisation, to test whether the interpretation holds
3.5Evaluate the limits of what the data can show, and what would be needed to settle the question
3.6Identify where an AI or automated tool was used in the analysis, and evaluate what was checked and why

Applied in Finance

3.1 and 3.2 analyse the data and interpret where the team's effort is going. 3.3 holds an alternative reading. A rise in late payments might reflect a billing error rather than weaker chasing. 3.4 tests the reading against comparable work. 3.5 states what the data cannot show. 3.6 records where AI was used, such as drafted commentary on the aged debt report, and what was checked.

LO4
The learner will: Be able to direct a department's priorities from what data indicates.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Determine the changes to the department's priorities that follow from the interpretation
4.2Evaluate what the department would stop or reduce in order to make the changes possible
4.3Consult the people whose work the changes would affect, and record what was raised
4.4Adapt the proposed changes in response to what the consultation established, and state what changed
4.5Present the proposed priorities, with the evidence, to the person who decides them, and respond to challenge
4.6State how the effect of the changes will be measured, and over what period

Applied in Finance

4.1 and 4.2 set the change in priorities and what the team would stop or reduce. A weekly report nobody uses is a typical candidate. 4.3 and 4.4 consult the people affected and adapt. 4.5 presents to the person who sets the team's priorities, and responds to challenge. 4.6 states how the effect will be measured, which may mean changing a measure the team reports.

LO5
The learner will: Be able to evaluate the effect of directing priorities from data.
3 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Evaluate the effect of the changed priorities against what was stated at 4.6, using evidence
5.2Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.4 was, giving reasons
5.3Identify what the department would measure differently, and what would be determined differently next time, and the reasons

Applied in Finance

5.1 evaluates the effect against 4.6, using at least one measurement taken after the change. 5.2 reviews the method set at 2.4. 5.3 identifies what the team would measure differently and what would be determined differently next time. One example is exception ageing in place of invoice counts.

5 learning outcomes, 25 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Finance work

  • 1.1, 1.2, 1.3. An annotated copy of the team's current measures. It states what each counts, over what period, what it encourages and what it leaves out.
  • 2.1, 2.2, 2.3. A note of the learner's question about the team's priorities and the data chosen. It records the data set aside and the effect of setting it aside.
  • 3.1, 3.2, 3.3. The analysis from the learner's own tools. It includes the alternative reading and why one is better supported.
  • 3.6. A declaration of where an AI tool was used in the analysis. It states what was checked against the ledger or source report, and why.
  • 4.3, 4.4, 4.5. Consultation notes and the revised proposal. A record of the challenge raised when it went to the decision maker.
  • 5.1, 5.3. A review against the measure stated at 4.6, using figures from after the change. It ends with what the team would measure differently.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when the learner is given the question and the monthly reporting pack to answer it from. It rises above Level 5 when the learner reconsiders what finance measures for, such as rewriting the organisation's performance measures. That is outside this unit.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-DA-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

ZFF-PJ-05

Applied Project: Annual Automation Plan for Own Department

Level5TQT140 hoursCredits14GLH10 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria30

In Finance

The brief is an annual automation plan for the learner's own finance function or team. The finance year gives it shape. There are month-end closes, quarter ends, year end and audit, budget setting, VAT returns and the payroll year end. Nothing else is given. The learner decides the processes, what counts as a benefit, the order, and whose agreement is needed.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Be able to establish what own department does and what it costs.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Determine the boundary of the department the plan will cover, and state the reasons for it
1.2Map the processes the department carries out across a year, including those that occur only occasionally
1.3Establish the volume, the time and the cost of each main process from the department's own systems
1.4Determine the method used to establish those figures, and state the reasons for choosing it
1.5Evaluate the reliability of the figures, and state how gaps and disputed figures were handled
1.6Identify the obligations and commitments the department must continue to meet whatever the plan changes

Applied in Finance

1.1 sets the boundary, such as transactional finance but not treasury. 1.2 maps processes across the year, including occasional ones such as audit requests and the budget round. 1.3 and 1.4 take volume, time and cost from the team's own systems, by a method the learner determines. 1.5 handles gaps and disputed figures. 1.6 lists the obligations the plan must keep meeting, such as VAT returns and payroll reporting.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to analyse which of a department's processes are candidates for automation.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Determine the criteria by which candidate processes will be selected, and state the reasons for them
2.2Analyse each main process against those criteria
2.3Interpret the cost and the benefit of automating each candidate, using the department's own figures
2.4Use relevant investigation of comparable work to inform the evaluation, and state what it established
2.5Identify the processes that should not be automated, and evaluate the reasons for each
2.6Evaluate the candidates against one another and state the order in which they are recommended

Applied in Finance

2.1 sets the learner's own criteria for selecting candidates. 2.2 and 2.3 analyse each main process and interpret its cost and benefit from the team's figures. 2.4 states what investigation of comparable work established. 2.5 names the processes that should stay manual, with reasons for each. 2.6 puts the candidates in order.

LO3
The learner will: Be able to consult the people whose work a plan would change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Identify the people whose work each recommended change would affect, and how it would affect them
3.2Consult those people, and record what was raised
3.3Analyse the concerns raised and the reasoning given for them, and evaluate which of them change the plan
3.4Adapt the plan in response, and state what changed and the reasons
3.5Evaluate the skills the department will need that it does not currently hold, and state how they will be obtained

Applied in Finance

3.1 and 3.2 identify and consult everyone whose work the plan changes. That includes clerks, budget holders who authorise spend and the payroll team. 3.3 and 3.4 analyse what was raised and adapt the plan. 3.5 evaluates the skills this plan needs and how they will be obtained. Maintaining rules on a matching tool is one example.

LO4
The learner will: Be able to produce a sequenced annual plan with checks and fallbacks.
7 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Sequence the recommended changes across the year, and state the reasons for the order
4.2Identify the dependencies between the changes, and between the changes and work outside the department
4.3State the resources each change requires, and when they are required
4.4State the checks that will be carried out on each change, by whom, and at what point
4.5State the fallback for each change, and the point at which the fallback would be used
4.6Evaluate the risks the plan carries for the department, and state what would be done about each
4.7Determine how the effect of each change will be measured, and against what starting figure

Applied in Finance

4.1 sequences the changes around the finance calendar, such as avoiding a go-live just before year end. 4.2 identifies dependencies, such as system changes owned by IT or the auditor's review of a new control. 4.3 states resources and when they are needed. 4.4 and 4.5 state the checks, who does them, and fallbacks such as a manual payment run. 4.6 evaluates risks. 4.7 sets each starting figure.

LO5
The learner will: Be able to present a departmental plan and evaluate own method.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Present the plan to the person who signs off the department's plans, in a form suited to that decision
5.2Respond to challenge on the plan's figures, its sequence and its risks
5.3Record the decision taken and any conditions attached to it
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 1.4 and the criteria determined at 2.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Evaluate how far the consultation changed the plan, giving reasons
5.6Identify what would be determined differently in the next annual plan, and the reasons

Applied in Finance

5.1 and 5.2 present the plan to the person who signs off the department's plans, such as the finance director. The learner responds to challenge on figures, sequence and risks. 5.3 records the decision and any conditions. 5.4 to 5.6 review the method and criteria, how far consultation changed the plan, and what to change next year.

5 learning outcomes, 30 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Finance work

  • 1.1, 1.2, 1.6. A boundary statement and a year map of the team's processes, including audit requests. It lists the obligations the plan must keep meeting.
  • 1.3, 1.4, 1.5. A cost base for each main process from the team's own systems. The method is stated and disputed figures are resolved or flagged.
  • 2.1, 2.5, 2.6. The learner's selection criteria and the ordered list of candidates. The processes kept manual are listed with reasons.
  • 3.2, 3.3, 3.4. Consultation records with colleagues identified by role. A change log shows how the plan moved in response.
  • 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5. The plan itself, sequenced against the team's own close calendar. Each change carries its dependencies, checks, owners and fallback.
  • 5.1, 5.2, 5.3. Witness testimony of the presentation and a note of the challenge raised. The recorded decision, with any conditions.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when a transformation team supplies the process list, the selection criteria or a business case template that fixes what counts as a benefit. It rises above Level 5 when the plan reshapes how the organisation runs finance, such as centralising processing across the group. That belongs at 4.2 as a dependency outside the department.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-PJ-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

Section 5

Assessment

This version is assessed exactly as the generic Diploma: by portfolio from real work, decided by a human assessor, with a recorded professional discussion for every unit. See assessment and quality assurance and the evidence trail on the generic Diploma.

Section 6

What we know is not yet right

Listed plainly, so that a reviewer has this list before finding any of it.

1

No finance practitioner, and no assessor with finance experience, has read this version yet.

2

Many finance teams work under an internal control framework that lists each process's controls. An assessor needs to confirm it may inform the constraints at ZFF-AU-05 1.4. It must not become the criteria at ZFF-AU-05 3.1 or ZFF-PJ-05 2.1.

3

The rules named here apply to most UK finance teams. Sector rules, such as those for financial services firms or public bodies, are not covered and may add constraints.

4

Everything open on the generic Diploma applies here too. See its open items.
